legend: A widely known among some people Belarusian sport programmer Yura possesses lots of information about cars. That is why he has been invited to participate in a game show called "Guess That Car!".

The game show takes place on a giant parking lot, which is 4n meters long from north to south and 4m meters wide from west to east. The lot has n + 1 dividing lines drawn from west to east and m + 1 dividing lines drawn from north to south, which divide the parking lot into n·m 4 by 4 meter squares. There is a car parked strictly inside each square. The dividing lines are numbered from 0 to n from north to south and from 0 to m from west to east. Each square has coordinates (i, j) so that the square in the north-west corner has coordinates (1, 1) and the square in the south-east corner has coordinates (n, m). See the picture in the notes for clarifications.

Before the game show the organizers offer Yura to occupy any of the (n + 1)·(m + 1) intersection points of the dividing lines. After that he can start guessing the cars. After Yura chooses a point, he will be prohibited to move along the parking lot before the end of the game show. As Yura is a car expert, he will always guess all cars he is offered, it's just a matter of time. Yura knows that to guess each car he needs to spend time equal to the square of the euclidean distance between his point and the center of the square with this car, multiplied by some coefficient characterizing the machine's "rarity" (the rarer the car is, the harder it is to guess it). More formally, guessing a car with "rarity" c placed in a square whose center is at distance d from Yura takes c·d2 seconds. The time Yura spends on turning his head can be neglected.
It just so happened that Yura knows the "rarity" of each car on the parking lot in advance. Help him choose his point so that the total time of guessing all cars is the smallest possible.
input: The first line contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ n, m ≤ 1000) — the sizes of the parking lot. Each of the next n lines contains m integers: the j-th number in the i-th line describes the "rarity" cij (0 ≤ cij ≤ 100000) of the car that is located in the square with coordinates (i, j).
output: In the first line print the minimum total time Yura needs to guess all offered cars. In the second line print two numbers li and lj (0 ≤ li ≤ n, 0 ≤ lj ≤ m) — the numbers of dividing lines that form a junction that Yura should choose to stand on at the beginning of the game show. If there are multiple optimal starting points, print the point with smaller li. If there are still multiple such points, print the point with smaller lj.
Please do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use the cin, cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
note: In the first test case the total time of guessing all cars is equal to 3·8 + 3·8 + 4·8 + 9·8 + 5·40 + 1·40 = 392.

output.ai: 第一行输出 Yura 猜出所有提供的汽车所需的最短总时间。第二行输出两个数 li 和 lj（0 ≤ li ≤ n，0 ≤ lj ≤ m）——构成 Yura 应在游戏节目开始时选择站立的交点的两条分界线的编号。如果有多个最优起点，输出 li 较小的点。如果仍有多个这样的点，输出 lj 较小的点。
请不要在 C++ 中使用 %lld 格式说明符来读写 64 位整数。建议使用 cin、cout 流或 %I64d 格式说明符。

note.ai: 在第一个测试用例中，猜出所有汽车的总时间等于 3·8 + 3·8 + 4·8 + 9·8 + 5·40 + 1·40 = 392。

legend.ai: 在某些人群中广为人知的白俄罗斯竞赛程序员 Yura 掌握着大量关于汽车的信息。因此，他受邀参加名为“猜猜这辆车！”的游戏节目。

游戏节目在一个巨大的停车场中举行，该停车场从北到南长 4n 米，从西到东宽 4m 米。停车场中有 n + 1 条从西向东绘制的分界线，以及 m + 1 条从北向南绘制的分界线，它们将停车场划分为 n·m 个 4×4 米的方格。每个方格内（严格不在边界上）都停放着一辆汽车。分界线从北到南编号为 0 至 n，从西到东编号为 0 至 m。每个方格都有坐标 (i, j)，其中西北角的方格坐标为 (1, 1)，东南角的方格坐标为 (n, m)。具体说明请参见题目注释中的图片。

在游戏节目开始前，主办方允许 Yura 占据分界线交点中的任意一个，即 (n + 1)·(m + 1) 个交点中的任意一个。之后，他就可以开始猜车了。Yura 选定一个点后，在游戏节目结束前都不允许在停车场内移动。由于 Yura 是汽车专家，他总能猜出节目提供的所有汽车，只是需要一定的时间。Yura 知道，猜出每辆汽车所需的时间等于他所在点与该汽车所在方格中心之间的欧几里得距离的平方，再乘以一个表示汽车“稀有度”的系数（汽车越稀有，就越难猜出）。更正式地说，对于一辆“稀有度”为 c、停放在中心到 Yura 的距离为 d 的方格中的汽车，猜出它所需的时间为 c·d² 秒。Yura 转头所花费的时间可以忽略不计。
碰巧，Yura 事先知道停车场中每辆汽车的“稀有度”。请帮助他选择一个点，使猜出所有汽车所需的总时间尽可能短。

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 n 和 m（1 ≤ n, m ≤ 1000），表示停车场的大小。接下来的 n 行中，每行包含 m 个整数：第 i 行中的第 j 个数描述了坐标为 (i, j) 的方格中汽车的“稀有度” cij（0 ≤ cij ≤ 100000）。
